Formulation:
Predisposing: Young adult living alone; family history of atopy may predispose to skin irritation contributing to distress.  
Precipitating: Recent classroom difficulties, long work hours, possible irritant dermatitis after swimming.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing workplace stress, fatigue, pruritus interfering with comfort.  
Protective: Stable employment, absence of substance misuse, willingness to seek medical advice.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Work-related stress
- Patient Goal(s): Feel less stressed at work; improve overall well-being.
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce subjective stress and fatigue; prevent progression to anxiety/depressive disorder.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Implement stress-management strategies (e.g., scheduled breaks, relaxation techniques).  
  • Maintain regular sleep and hydration.  
  • Monitor stress triggers and skin symptoms; return if worsening.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief psychoeducation on stress and coping.  
  • Offer information on mindfulness apps/local stress-management workshops.  
  • Review in 4–6 weeks; consider referral to psychologist or EAP if stress persists.

Secondary Problem: Occupational burnout risk
- Patient Goal(s): Restore healthy work–life balance.
- Clinical Goal(s): Prevent burnout; maintain function and job satisfaction.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Set realistic work boundaries; discuss workload with leadership if feasible.  
  • Engage in regular physical activity for stress relief.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Supply supporting medical letter if workplace adjustments needed.  
  • Screen for mood/anxiety disorders at follow-up.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Relationship between stress and physical symptoms; healthy coping strategies; when to seek further help.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating fatigue, mood changes, sleep disturbance, persistent pruritus despite dermatologic treatment.
- Coping Strategies: Relaxation breathing, scheduled leisure time, social support, moisturising regimen to reduce skin discomfort.
